title: QQQI Ex-Dividend Date Is Nov 18. Here’s The Math For A 32-Year-Old Who Wants $1,000 A Month
detail:
QQQI Ex-Dividend Date Is Nov 18. Here’s The Math For A 32-Year-Old Who Wants $1,000 A Month
AJ Tiarsmith
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 10:23 AM CST 5 min read
QQQI
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Generating $1,000 monthly from QQQI requires roughly $79,000, versus about $2.7 million for QQQ.

The 14% distribution rate rests on covered-call premiums, not dividends, and NEOS classified nearly all October's payout as return of capital that shrinks cost basis.

Covered calls cap upside: QQQI returned 8% this year versus 13% for the Nasdaq-100, so a 32-year-old forfeits growth by taking income now.

Americans who work with a financial advisor have saved more than twice as much for retirement, on average. Find out what one could change for you: SmartAsset's free quiz matches you with up to three vetted fiduciary advisors in about five minutes. (Sponsor)

The NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (NASDAQ:QQQI) announces its next payout on Nov. 17, 2026, goes ex-dividend on Nov. 18 and pays on Nov. 20, according to NEOS Investments' distribution calendar. NEOS sets November's amount in that declaration, and the figure wasn't posted when this was written.

pixelfit / E+ via Getty Images

The ex-dividend date is the cutoff for qualifying, and the record date is when the fund checks its shareholder list. Both fall on Nov. 18, so an investor has to buy before that day. Buying on or after Nov. 18 misses November's check.

To make the math specific, take an simple example: a single investor, age 32, still working, investing through a taxable brokerage account, who wants $1,000 a month.

What $1,000 a Month From QQQI Costs Right Now

With November not yet declared, the math uses October's payout. September paid $0.6339 and August paid $0.6518, so the check moves each month.

Item

Annual income

Other yield levels show the range. At a typical 3.5% dividend growth yield, $12,000 over 0.035 works out to about $342,857. At a typical 6% from REITs or preferred shares, $12,000 divided by 0.06 is $200,000. At the 0.45% yield StockAnalysis lists for the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), it takes about $2.7 million.

------

Can You Answer These Three Questions?

Americans say they need $1.46 million to retire comfortably. Whether that number fits your life depends on three questions most people never work through:

1. How much can you withdraw each year without running out?

2. When should you claim Social Security?

3. How much will taxes take from your 401(k) or IRA?
